trials.label: r1c1
trials.name: Footprint-conv placement head
trials.hypothesis: Keep the baseline body, but replace the 1x1 placement head with one small conv per brick type. Its kernel is the brick's footprint (dy x dx), anchored top-left, then ReLU and a 1x1 output. Each logit then directly combines every cell the brick would cover, which makes it easier to learn the landing height (max over the footprint) and target match. Compute is about 1.35x. Refuted if dev success is no better than the baseline's.

trials.label: r1c2
trials.name: Residual body + global broadcast
trials.hypothesis: Residual 3x3 blocks, a broadcast of global (mean+max) context mid-network and per-footprint window heads let each brick's logit see every cell it covers and the overall build progress. The output layers start at zero, so all untrained logits are equal and the net has no placement bias before training. Refuted if dev success is no better than the baseline's after compute matching.

trials.label: r1c3
trials.name: 3D voxel encoder
trials.hypothesis: Reshape the build/target/missing/extra channels into a [4, Z, Y, X] voxel grid. Add a constant layer-index channel and copy the height and time planes to every layer. Run two 3x3x3 conv layers (16 channels), fold Z into channels with a 1x1 conv, add global broadcast, then the footprint head. The 3D convs let the network relate a cell to the layers directly above and below, where bricks land and overhangs seal cells. Compute is about 1.5x. Refuted if it scores worse than the 2D candidates or the baseline, or runs too slowly.

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

C3 = 16
WIDTH = 64
HID = 32


class FootprintHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.convs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(c, hid, (dy, dx)) for dy, dx in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), conv, out in zip(self.fps, self.convs, self.outs):
            h = F.relu(conv(F.pad(f, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Z = int(spec.Z)
        zc = torch.arange(self.Z, dtype=torch.float32) / max(self.Z - 1, 1)
        self.register_buffer("zc", zc.view(1, 1, self.Z, 1, 1))
        self.c3a = nn.Conv3d(8, C3, 3, padding=1)
        self.c3b = nn.Conv3d(C3, C3, 3, padding=1)
        self.fold = nn.Conv2d(C3 * self.Z, WIDTH, 1)
        self.mid_glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(WIDTH, WIDTH))
        self.head = FootprintHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, C, Y, X = obs.shape
        Z = self.Z
        vox = obs[:, :4 * Z].reshape(B, 4, Z, Y, X)
        planes = obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 3].unsqueeze(2).expand(B, 3, Z, Y, X)
        zc = self.zc.expand(B, 1, Z, Y, X)
        v = torch.cat([vox, planes, zc], dim=1)
        h = F.relu(self.c3a(v))
        h = F.relu(self.c3b(h))
        f = F.relu(self.fold(h.reshape(B, C3 * Z, Y, X)))
        gm = self.mid_glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        f = F.relu(f + gm[:, :, None, None])
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

trials.label: r2c1
trials.name: Footprint min/max/mean pooling head
trials.hypothesis: Keep the baseline body. Replace the 1x1 placement head with a learned 1x1 projection, then max, min and mean pooling over each brick's footprint (anchored top-left), then a per-type 1x1 MLP. Max-pooling learned height features gives the landing layer, and min-pooling learned 'missing' features gives the AND over all covered cells. Cost is about 1.3x, cheaper than footprint convs for big bricks. Refuted if it scores no better than the baseline and r1c1.

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 64
PROJ = 32
HID = 32


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.body = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import math
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

D = 64
HEADS = 4
PROJ = 32
HID = 32


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Block(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d, heads):
        super().__init__()
        self.h = heads
        self.ln1 = nn.LayerNorm(d)
        self.qkv = nn.Linear(d, 3 * d)
        self.o = nn.Linear(d, d)
        self.ln2 = nn.LayerNorm(d)
        self.mlp = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(d, 2 * d), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(2 * d, d))

    def forward(self, x):
        B, N, Dm = x.shape
        hd = Dm // self.h
        qkv = self.qkv(self.ln1(x)).reshape(B, N, 3, self.h, hd).permute(2, 0, 3, 1, 4)
        q, k, v = qkv.unbind(0)
        a = torch.softmax(torch.matmul(q, k.transpose(-2, -1)) / math.sqrt(hd), dim=-1)
        y = torch.matmul(a, v).transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, N, Dm)
        x = x + self.o(y)
        return x + self.mlp(self.ln2(x))


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        n = int(spec.Y) * int(spec.X)
        self.stem = nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, D, 3, padding=1)
        self.pos = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(1, n, D) * 0.02)
        self.block = Block(D, HEADS)
        self.head = PoolHead(D, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * D, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, C, Y, X = obs.shape
        h = F.relu(self.stem(obs))
        t = h.flatten(2).transpose(1, 2) + self.pos
        t = self.block(t)
        f = F.relu(t.transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, D, Y, X))
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c3 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=2, dilation=2)
        self.c4 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.mid_glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(WIDTH, WIDTH))
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        x = F.relu(self.c1(obs))
        x = x + F.relu(self.c2(x))
        gm = self.mid_glob(torch.cat([x.mean((2, 3)), x.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        x = x + gm[:, :, None, None]
        x = x + F.relu(self.c3(x))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c4(x))
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 64
PROJ = 32
HID = 32


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.gproj = nn.Linear(2 * c, hid)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        for o in self.outs:
            nn.init.orthogonal_(o.weight, gain=0.01)
            nn.init.zeros_(o.bias)

    def forward(self, f, gfeat):
        p = self.proj(f)
        gb = self.gproj(gfeat)[:, :, None, None]
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)) + gb)
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.body = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        nn.init.orthogonal_(self.done_head.weight, gain=0.01)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.done_head.bias)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        gfeat = torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1)
        place = self.head(f, gfeat)
        g = self.glob(gfeat)
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c3 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.mid_glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(WIDTH, WIDTH))
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        x = F.relu(self.c1(obs))
        x = x + F.relu(self.c2(x))
        gm = self.mid_glob(torch.cat([x.mean((2, 3)), x.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        x = x + gm[:, :, None, None]
        f = F.relu(x + self.c3(x))
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

trials.label: r4c3
trials.name: Per-column MLP stem + pooled head
trials.hypothesis: A two-layer 1x1-conv MLP (64 then 48 channels) first processes each column's full layer stack: build, target, missing, extra and heights. This makes per-column rules easy to learn, such as 'the next missing layer is exactly at build height' or 'an extra cell blocks this column'. Two 3x3 layers (width 40) and the footprint pooling head follow. Cost is about 1.0x, so it trains the full budget. Refuted if it scores no better than r3c1, whose first layer mixes space and layers at once.
trials.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        s = self.stem(obs)
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.1: There are no results yet, so this round is about spreading the bets. The task: each placement logit has to tell whether a brick, dropped onto the highest cell under its footprint, fills target cells at that layer and seals nothing it shouldn't. In the baseline, a 1x1 head reads one cell's features, so the footprint's other cells (and so the landing height) have to be squeezed into each anchor's features. Ordering needs global context too (e.g. are the supports for an overhang still missing?), and the baseline's placement head never sees any. I propose three candidates. (1) A footprint-shaped placement head on the baseline body: one main change, cheap. (2) A deeper residual body with global features added back into every cell, plus the footprint head, at about 1.5x compute. (3) A new idea: a 3D voxel encoder that relates layers directly, plus global broadcast and the footprint head. All three stay at or under about 1.5x compute so the step budget stays reasonable. Scores are hidden, so every candidate rests on its own reasoning.
analyses.2:
Scores are hidden, so the only evidence is that all three round-1 designs trained within limits: the footprint-conv head (1.4x compute), the residual body with a global broadcast (1.63x) and the 3D voxel encoder (1.52x). I can't rank them. The best plan is a set of different, cheap ideas that each fit the task, since the top 3 trials by real dev score go on to more seeds.

The decisive check for each action is an AND over the brick's footprint: the landing layer is the highest stack under the footprint, and every covered cell must be missing at that layer. After a learned layer, I can approximate this with max, min and mean pooling over the footprint, which is cheaper than footprint convs. With so few steps, cheap networks get the full budget and may win.

This round tests that pooled head on the baseline body, on a conv+attention hybrid with global reach, and on a deeper, narrow residual body with dilation.
analyses.3: All six trials trained without errors, but no scores are shown, so I can only reason from priors. I can't say yet which of the ideas tried so far helped. Five of the six trials cost 1.3–1.6x the starting network's compute, so each trained on 70–76% of the starting network's environment steps. In short-budget PPO, more steps often matter more than extra capacity. The footprint pooling head (max, min and mean over a brick's cells) is the cheapest way I have found to let each logit see all the cells its brick covers, and it fits how bricks land. For this round: (1) a slimmer pooled-head network that costs under 1x, so it gets the full 131k steps; (2) the current pooled-head network with whole-board context fed into the head and near-zero initial policy outputs, a standard PPO choice; (3) a new idea, gated (multiplicative) convolutions, which make AND-style rules easy to learn, such as 'target filled at this layer AND build height equals this layer'. Spreading the candidates out improves the odds that the final top-3 includes a strong design.
analyses.4: I can't see any scores, so none of the 9 trials can be ranked, and none can be called a failure. Every trial trained without errors, so even the 1.6x designs fit the time limit. Of the ideas I think matter most, two keep coming back: placement heads that pool over a brick's footprint (one logit combines every cell the brick covers), and global context for each placement. The other factor I can control is how many steps a network gets: networks costing about 1x or less train the full 131k steps. In this last round I spread risk across three cheap (about 1x) changes. Each sits close to r3c1 (the lean pooled head at width 48), so each result has a clear reading. (1) r3c1 plus global conditioning in the head and a small output init: the r3c2 idea at full budget. (2) r3c1 plus one more residual layer and a mid-network global broadcast: depth at full budget. (3) A new idea: a per-column 1x1 MLP stem, so the network learns per-cell layer logic (height against target, missing and extra cells) before spatial mixing.
